policy_context.resource_basis: A distinct one-shot follow-up to the consumed writer_group_commit_flush_reader_pair. That operation showed the default arm's post-writer explicit Flush had no pending delta and did not exercise metadata staging; do not infer reader-through-flush impact from its default-arm trace. This profile compares ordinary Upsert with bounded four-record/500-us Upsert group commit while both use metadata staging, with 8,192 seed documents and 32 concurrent logical writes. Immediately before the continuous-reader phase, each arm applies a separate 256-document WAL-durable batch with unique flushmarker terms; this intentionally leaves a bounded pending delta below max_delta_docs so the explicit Flush must persist real data. Verify exactly 256 flushmarker hits after close/reopen. Timestamp two continuously active readers across that flush; require at least two completed queries before/after, a started+overlapping query during it, phase-log corroboration, pending_flush_ms and nonzero segment build/write work. Preserve atomic publication and WAL durability. Capture writer/group queue and fsync metrics, reader wall/mutex/CPU, flush stages/locks, bytes, cgroup/host resource and I/O evidence. New profile, not retry or reuse of the prior one; any gate/containment/overlap/flush-work check failure consumes it without retry. Exploratory only; no stable-tail, architecture, qualification or production claim.
policy_context.risk_acceptance_reference: The standard contention profile is four-arm; writer_group_commit is a separate two-arm per-call Upsert experiment. All are descriptive only: shared-host pressure, one round per arm and test-scale workloads prohibit causal, qualification or architecture-win claims. ApplyBatch and Upsert call latencies have different units and must not be compared as equivalent tail samples.
